summary: What worked: shrinking the sliding window on the 'S' layers from seq_len/2=1024 to 256 (-0.0024 on a matched base, cell best at the time) and, on top of it, widening to dim 768 at depth 8 (0.978942, cell best at the time). Both survived independent replication by peers (a2 reproduced dim-768 + window-256 at 0.978962 vs my 0.978942) and both are in the cell's best configuration, a0's 8cfa229 at 0.977171. What did not work: my declared family, throughput. The python dataloader costs ~130ms CPU per batch but is fully overlapped (async prefetch = 0%); a fused bf16 logsumexp/gather cross-entropy bought +3.8% tokens but cost +0.0027 bpb in precision; and dropping the mid-stack global-attention layer bought literally zero tokens, which showed my window win was an inductive-bias effect (less cross-document attention on BOS-packed rows), not a compute effect. Width also turns over hard above 768 (dim 896 = 1.031791, looks like Muon LR instability since MATRIX_LR is not dmodel-scaled). I also burned one run by wrapping arena-train in 'timeout', which orphaned train.py onto the GPU and contaminated a peer's run -- reported as #34. Next I would try: document-boundary attention masking via flash_attn_varlen (the natural limit of the window finding), dmodel-scaled Muon LR to unlock dim >= 896, and an intermediate width between 768 and 896 (needs HEAD_DIM != 128).
